title: Global e-Waste Monitor 2024: Electronic Waste Rising Five Times Faster than Documented E-waste Recycling
book_use: Chs. 1, 5, 19, and 24: scale and growth of e-waste; evidence that physical replacement creates collection, reuse, recycling, and disposal tails. Used with explicit caution that e-waste does not prove the full book thesis.

title: The Global E-waste Monitor 2024
book_use: Chs. 1 and 5: cross-check for 2022 global e-waste generation and documented formal collection/recycling; product end-of-life context.

title: RFC 8996: Deprecating TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1
book_use: Chs. 2, 11, 15, 19, 23, and 25: concrete deprecation case showing maintenance/security benefits alongside interoperability costs for legacy users.

title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679, Article 17 — Right to erasure ('right to be forgotten')
book_use: Chs. 3 and 22: defined erasure rights and explicit exceptions; used to distinguish deletion rights from universal erasure or historical amnesia.

title: Scheduling Records
book_use: Chs. 3 and 22: records schedules distinguish permanent from temporary records and show that legitimate preservation and deliberate destruction are both lifecycle decisions.

title: Understanding Federal Legislation: A Section-by-Section Guide to Key Legal Considerations
book_use: Ch. 4: sunset provisions as mechanisms that terminate authority at a future time and force a decision about extension, amendment, or lapse; not evidence that sunsets automatically improve policy.

title: Sunset Act of 1977, S. 2
book_use: Chs. 4 and 13: historical evidence that systematic sunset/review proposals require schedules, information, scope, and oversight rather than mere dates.

title: Plan Ahead for Phase Out of 3G Cellular Networks and Service
book_use: Chs. 5 and 23: network shutdowns can strand phones and embedded connected devices, illustrating migration and last-user costs without implying shutdown itself is wrongful.

title: Apoptosis: A Review of Programmed Cell Death
book_use: Ch. 6: regulated cell death in development, tissue homeostasis, and immune function; used strictly as a bounded biological analogy with dysregulation counterexamples.

author_or_institution: U.S. Forest Service Research and Development
title: Prescribed Fire
book_use: Ch. 7: prescribed fire as a context-dependent ecological management tool that can maintain or restore ecosystem conditions and reduce certain wildfire risks; supports careful limits on the metaphor.

title: Why Forget? On the Adaptive Value of Memory Loss
book_use: Ch. 8: adaptive functions of forgetting including abstraction, emotional regulation, and context-sensitive memory use; not used to equate human memory with institutional deletion.

author_or_institution: Tomás J. Ryan / Paul W. Frankland
title: Forgetting as a form of adaptive engram cell plasticity
book_use: Ch. 8: contemporary neuroscience framing some forgetting as adaptive rather than simple system failure.

author_or_institution: Michael C. Anderson / Justin C. Hulbert
title: Active Forgetting: Adaptation of Memory by Prefrontal Control
book_use: Ch. 8: evidence and theory on active control processes that reduce memory accessibility; supports distinction between active forgetting and passive decay.

author_or_institution: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts
title: Process — Bankruptcy Basics
book_use: Ch. 9: bankruptcy's fresh-start function and the legal organization of financial failure; used with chapter-specific caveats about debt types, liens, and different proceedings.

author_or_institution: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts
title: Discharge in Bankruptcy — Bankruptcy Basics
book_use: Ch. 9: discharge releases a debtor from personal liability for specified debts and limits collection, while not all debts are dischargeable and some liens may survive.

author_or_institution: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Investor.gov
title: Options
book_use: Ch. 10: basic example of a time-bounded financial contract where expiration is part of the instrument; used only for mechanics, not as a universal market-design analogy.

title: Decommissioning Process
book_use: Chs. 1, 12, 24, and 25: reactor decommissioning as a staged process after permanent cessation, illustrating that operational stop and completed ending are different states.

title: Frequently Asked Questions About Reactor Decommissioning
book_use: Ch. 12: supplementary detail on notification, planning, fuel removal, and regulatory obligations after shutdown; used as a high-stakes case rather than a template for ordinary products.

title: Preparing Disposition Instructions
book_use: Chs. 14 and 25: retention periods and final disposition instructions; supports the distinctions among active use, archive, transfer, deletion, and destruction.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: SP 800-88 Rev. 2: Guidelines for Media Sanitization
book_use: Chs. 14 and 24: secure sanitization as a defined lifecycle function and evidence that destruction is a controlled process rather than a UI gesture.

title: AI Index Report 2026 — Economy
book_use: Ch. 16: broad context for AI adoption and investment; used only to ground the expansion of AI use, not to infer that every generated artifact becomes persistent infrastructure.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
book_use: Chs. 17, 18, and 25: AI lifecycle risk management and explicit decommissioning considerations, including dependencies, retained artifacts, security, and human factors.

title: Fiduciary Access to Digital Assets Act, Revised
book_use: Chs. 20, 22, and 29: fiduciary access to digital assets after death or incapacity and deliberate limits around private electronic communications; supports bounded digital succession rather than blanket inheritance.

author_or_institution: Avinash K. Dixit / Robert S. Pindyck
title: Investment Under Uncertainty
book_use: Ch. 21: real-options logic as a rigorous basis for valuing delay, staged commitment, and preserved flexibility under uncertainty; not converted into an unsupported universal premium.

title: 2026 Annual Report — key-person risk disclosure
book_use: Ch. 26: contemporary public-company example explicitly describing dependence on a co-founder/CEO for vision, strategy, culture, products, and technology; used as evidence that founder dependence is recognized as a material business risk, not as proof that founder-led companies are poorly governed.

title: Best Practices for Reducing Reusing and Recycling Construction and Demolition Materials
book_use: Ch. 27: design for adaptability, disassembly, reuse, visible connections, modular components, accessible repair information, and the explicit limit that complete deconstruction is not always feasible.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — AC-2 Account Management
book_use: Ch. 28: account lifecycle controls require account managers, defined authorizations, disabling expired or no-longer-associated accounts, and auditing account changes; used as a credential-lifecycle baseline that agent retirement must extend beyond.

author_or_institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology
title: SP 800-63A-4 — Subscriber Accounts
book_use: Chs. 28 and 29: account suspension or termination can be triggered by death, legal instruments, inactivity, compromise, or cessation of identity services; supports the claim that identity systems already encode lifecycle states rather than indefinite technical continuity.

title: How to add a Legacy Contact for your Apple Account
book_use: Ch. 29: concrete example of selective posthumous access requiring an access key and death certificate, while excluding some purchased content and Keychain data; supports selective continuity rather than blanket inheritance.

title: About Inactive Account Manager
book_use: Ch. 29: user-configured inactivity periods can trigger notification or selective data sharing with designated contacts; demonstrates a platform-level transition state while also exposing dependence on platform policy and continued service.
